# The boundaries graded by the classical works on pauses

*Generated by `scripts/analyze_stops.py`. Data: `data/source/waqf/`, built from the OpenITI texts by `scripts/extract_waqf.py`.*

The phrase test that places every new boundary is this project's own reading. This report checks it against three classical judges:

- **al-Dānī** (d. 444 AH), *al-Muktafā fī al-Waqf wa-l-Ibtidāʾ*;
- **al-Ushmūnī** (d. c. 1100 AH), *Manār al-Hudā fī Bayān al-Waqf wa-l-Ibtidāʾ*;
- **al-Ṣafāqusī** (d. 1118 AH), *Ghayth al-Nafʿ*, whose note on the last word of every quarter gives its grade, how widely it is accepted, and the alternatives of the Maghāriba and the Mashāriqa.

The grades, strongest first: **تام** (complete: the next aya is independent in wording and meaning), **كاف** (sufficient: independent in wording, linked in meaning), **حسن** (good: a stop, but the next words depend on these), **جائز/صالح** (permissible), **ليس بوقف** (not a stop). A boundary is graded by the aya end before it, with the stronger grade where the two books differ. The end of a surah is a complete stop by convention («آخر السورة تام») and is counted on its own.

## 1. The extraction

- al-Muktafā grades **1,844** aya ends, Manār al-Hudā **5,265**; both grade 1,702.
- Where both grade an aya end they give the same grade 60% of the time, and grades at most one step apart 96% of the time. Two independent books, parsed independently, would not agree this well if the quotes were placed on the wrong ayat.
- Ghayth al-Nafʿ: the quarter-end note was located for **233** of 240 quarters.
- Quotes are matched to ayat by their consonant skeleton, so the imlāʾī spelling of the books matches the Uthmani text. Manār numbers its quotes; al-Muktafā's are placed in order inside their surah. The edition's typo «نام» for «تام» is read as «تام» (e.g. 25:20).

| تام | 162 | 68% | 173 | 72% |
| كاف | 30 | 13% | 36 | 15% |
| حسن | 3 | 1% | 3 | 1% |
| جائز/صالح | 1 | 0% | 3 | 1% |
| ليس بوقف | 1 | 0% | 0 | 0% |
| not graded | 2 | 1% | 3 | 1% |
| **surah end, تام or كاف** | **232** | **97%** | **230** | **96%** |


Both divisions end almost every quarter at a complete or sufficient stop: 96% of the new boundaries against 97% of the traditional ones. The new division, though drawn for balance, is placed as well by the classical grades as the one drawn by them; it has more تام stops and fewer surah ends.

### The traditional juz that open inside a dialogue

The phrase test puts these juz starts inside a passage. The books grade the aya end before them:

| start |  | grade | al-Muktafā | Manār |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 18:75 | juz start | كاف | – | كاف |
| 51:31 | juz start | تام | – | تام |
| 37:145 | hizb/quarter | كاف | – | كاف |


So a passage the phrase test keeps whole can still contain a sufficient stop. The phrase test is stricter than the classical grade: it asks that the next aya open a new subject, not only a new sentence.

## 3. al-Ṣafāqusī's quarters and the Madina Mushaf

Of the 233 quarter ends located, **194** are the Madina end. Ghayth grades the last word تام 184 times and كاف 48 times, and states how widely the end is accepted:

| consensus (بإجماع، اتفاقا، بلا خلاف) | 117 |
| well known or his choice (المشهور، الجمهور، عليه عملنا) | 99 |
| one region (المغاربة or المشارقة) | 3 |
| some (عند بعض، جماعة) | 13 |
| not stated | 1 |

## 4. New boundaries on traditional positions

76 of the new boundaries fall on a Madina quarter end and 10 more on an end that only al-Ṣafāqusī gives. The rest are new positions, chosen for balance among the complete stops.
